url_verifier not run separately (same large-PDF class as the register); downloaded directly and confirmed via pdftotext -layout. Document title: 'Tariff Review of Integrated Natural Gas Pipeline (INGPL) of GAIL (India) Limited for determining Unit Natural Gas Pipeline tariff under the ... (Determination of Natural Gas Pipeline Tariff) Regulations, 2008.' Its opening pipeline-list table (line 14) shows 'Chhainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar 455' as one of the seven named trunk systems making up GAIL's 13,929.99 km INGPL transmission network, alongside HVJ-GREP-DVPL and JHBDPL -- undisputed transmission trunk lines. The whole 85-page order is a natural-gas TRANSMISSION tariff determination (repeated references to GAIL's 'natural gas transmission business/segment', e.g. lines 722, 730, 1084-1105).

resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources are PNGRB (regulator), so not independent of each other -- medium tier, single strong origin family. No source states the word 'transmission' against this specific pipeline's name, but the regulatory categorization is unambiguous: PNGRB authorises and tariffs CJHPL under its Natural Gas Pipeline Tariff Regulations as part of GAIL's Integrated Natural Gas Pipeline transmission network, the same regime and grouping as HVJ-GREP-DVPL/JHBDPL. This matches the deep-sweep audit shard's independent conclusion that PipelineType=transmission is correct (common-carrier trunk network, not gathering/process line).

VALUE DISAGREEMENT, not a missing-source gap -- do not stage a ref for StartYear1=2023. PNGRB's Nov-2025 INGPL tariff order (pngrb.gov.in/pdf/orders/20251127_TariffOrder.pdf, confirmed via pdftotext -layout after url_verifier's large-PDF false negative) lists 'Chainsa-Jhajjar-Hissar' with 'Date of Commissioning: 27-03-2010' in its economic-life table (line 338), used there to set the pipeline's tariff amortisation start -- 13 years before GEM's StartYear1=2023. The order's volume tables also show it already carrying gas in FY2022-23 (1.78 MMSCMD, line 2933) and FY2023-24 (2.03 MMSCMD, line 3134), i.e. flowing well before 2023. Its authorisation-history line (line 95) shows five separate authorisation actions for this pipeline -- 13.12.2010 (original), then resizing/extension actions on 12.06.2019, 29.09.2020, 17.12.2021, 20.06.2022 and 23.11.2022 -- so a 2022/2023-ish date could plausibly mark a LATEST EXTENSION reaching full 455 km rather than initial commissioning, which would reconcile with GEM's 2023 under a different definition of 'start'; the deep-sweep audit shard independently found the same open question (2016 PNGRB report: only 265/455 km built; May 2026 report: 440/455 km, no residual length flagged Under Construction). But no source states outright '2023' as a start/commission year for this pipeline, and the only source that gives a discrete commissioning date (27-03-2010) conflicts with the sheet by over a decade. Per standing rules, this is a value conflict routed to Update, not a ref to add here -- leaving StartYear1 unresolved and flagging the conflict rather than silently citing a source that disagrees with the recorded value.
